Answer: B
Reason: Comparing the initial chest X-ray (Figure 1a), which shows a focal opacity in the right mid-to-lower lung, with the later image (Figure 4), there is clear progression with increased density in the right lung and the appearance of new patchy opacities in the left lung. This pattern of progressive, multifocal airspace disease without cavitation or rapid resolution is characteristic of adenocarcinoma in situ (formerly bronchioloalveolar carcinoma), which can mimic pneumonia but fails to resolve and spreads.
